title: Recording fees and the manager Johnny Collins
summary: Randolph thinks the band was shortchanged on the cartoon, short and records by Collins, whom he and DeMichael suspect was a crook; Glaser later paid off Collins.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: To go back to the recording session, before you went off to New York. Do you remember what the recording fee was, what the scale was for recording?

Well, I -- to really tell you the truth, the recording fee -- I don't think we really got due justice on it, because Mike -- as I told you, I had charge of the arranging part of it, and directing the music -- I mean, the music director, and Mike had done most of the managing, like getting the uniforms and going between the men and the boss.
And the manager -- Louis says, "I know you told the --" McKendrick Louis told Mike McKinley, he say, "I know you boys are really
It meant that we -- that you had plenty of money, that you made plenty of money.

See, so you made the Betty Boop cartoon, and you made the 'Rhapsody in Black and Blue,' then you had the recording session on top of that. And Mike told him, said, and all of that. Said, we only got -- I forgot how much that Mike told him that we got. Anyway, it wasn't enough to write home about. And, see, that was in the manager -- that was the manager's doings. The manager did that. He gypped me out of that money.
Johnny Collins has a pretty bad reputation. Was he a crook?
Or had connections with Capone and people like that?
I don't know. He must have been, because I remember, Joe Glaser said -- or, he says, 'I paid Collins the last that I owe him now.'
This was later, when he took over the band.
When he took over, yes. Because when Collins booked Louis over in London the last time I was with

the band, booked him over there, Louis said that he put Scotland Yard out looking for Collins. And they said Collins didn't even dock. He was on the boat with Louis, and when the time come, why, Louis was looking for him and he didn't even dock. He just went on back.

And then, when Louis came back and got the band together and everything like that, that's when Canetti Cossette came in there, I think, while Louis was going from London and going to France and all that, and booking himself and getting a manager. And then, when Louis came back and he started to work in Collins' -- he attached -- that's what you call it, attached the box office?
Yeah. So Joe said -- I remember -- he said, "Well, we're free of Collins. I just paid Mr. Collins the last that we owe him."
It's funny how musicians get all messed up with people like that.
